payload.reason: TRL-0187 refuted BRN-goal-guard's approver clause: no premise said a human commit approves a policy, or that a reported agent commit withdraws that approval.

payload.proposed_statement: A project that enables the harness runs it as one release published it, and the harness measures that project: it reads that project's declarations and ledger, and runs that project's tests in that project's environment, not in the harness's own.
payload.reason: TRL-0190/0191: the enabling project was not tied to the measured one, and the environment clause did not say the harness's own is excluded.

payload.proposed_statement: Current trial: A trial is current exactly when three things hold: its validity, after any amendments appended to it, is valid; its target is in the premise graph; and the fingerprints it recorded -- one for each node by its id, its target and each node its target then depended on -- are exactly those its target and the nodes it now depends on have now, id for id: the same ids, and for each id the same fingerprint. A trial made before trials carried fingerprints counts as having recorded those its target and the nodes its target depended on had in the build when it was made. A node's fingerprint is determined by its statement and the premises it cites, and differs whenever either differs. Only current trials are counted, toward sufficiency, consensus and refutation alike.
payload.reason: A trial made before fingerprints stayed current after any restatement upstream, which AXM-blast-radius-invalidation forbids; 104 such trials exist across three projects. Judge them by the fingerprints their nodes had when they were made.

payload.proposed_statement: A project that enables the plugin at a version runs the release that plugin's manifest names, as it was published. Every server the plugin starts measures that project: it reads that project's declarations and ledger, and runs that project's tests in that project's environment, not in the harness's own.
payload.reason: TRL-0208/0209: "one release" let a plugin whose servers pin an older tag satisfy the axiom; and the axiom spoke of the harness, not each server.

payload.proposed_statement: A design is adopted only while the measurement it cites agrees with it. The measurement a design cites is each contract its derivation rule names as evidence, each read on its own; it agrees with the design when every one of them reads in the state the design's policy requires, and contradicts it when one reads refuted where the policy requires another state. A design whose cited measurement contradicts it is rejected, and one whose cited measurement does not agree, is absent or cannot be read is not adopted.
payload.reason: TRL-0212: nothing tied 'the measurement it cites' to the contracts the derivation names, read one by one, or said when it agrees or contradicts.

payload.proposed_statement: A declaration takes effect only from the committed revision. Every verdict and every proof state the servers report is computed from committed content -- the declarations at the head revision, the commits that evidence names, and, for a trial made before trials carried fingerprints, the declarations committed when it was made -- and from the ledger, and from no other file in the working tree.
payload.reason: TRL-0207: as stated it bound every verdict, including the guard refusing a commit before it exists; it means the servers' verdicts. It also now names the committed history a legacy trial is judged by.

payload.proposed_statement: Making an edit to a declaration file, without committing it, changes no verdict and no proof state the servers report.
payload.reason: Follows AXM-commit-is-approval's narrowing to the verdicts and proof states the servers report.

payload.proposed_statement: Only committed declarations reach the belief model; no evidence recorded against a contract that no declared test can measure moves a belief; and making an uncommitted edit to a declaration file changes no verdict the servers report.
payload.reason: Follows AXM-commit-is-approval's narrowing to the verdicts the servers report.

payload.proposed_statement: Making an edit to a declaration file, and nothing else -- no commit, and no record appended to the ledger -- changes no verdict and no proof state the servers report.
payload.reason: TRL (pass 3) gap: a server writing a ledger entry triggered by the edit is a further change the derivation already excluded; the statement now says so.

payload.proposed_statement: A design is a branch, and adopting it is a decision on that branch under a policy criterion; the state that criterion requires of the branch's evidence is the state the design's policy requires. A design is adopted only while the measurement it cites agrees with it. The measurement a design cites is each contract its derivation rule names, each read on its own; it agrees with the design exactly when every one of them reads in the required state, and contradicts it exactly when one reads refuted where the required state is another. A design whose cited measurement contradicts it is rejected, and one whose cited measurement does not agree, is absent or cannot be read is not adopted.
payload.reason: Pass 3 gap: 'agrees when' read as only sufficient, and nothing tied a branch and a policy criterion's required state to a design and its policy.

payload.proposed_statement: Release: The release a plugin's manifest names is the code at the git tag tdlp--v<version>, where <version> is the version that manifest names -- the one its marketplace entry and the package name too. A project runs that release as it was published exactly when every server the plugin starts installs from that tag.
payload.reason: Pass 3 gap: 'runs as published when' read as only sufficient.

payload.proposed_statement: The human's commit of the goal set approves it and every policy it declares, and no other commit does. An agent commit that would change the goal set is refused; one that is made anyway is reported until the human next commits the goal set, and while one is reported no adoption under a policy goals.yaml declares stands as approved unless the human is named as its approver.
payload.reason: Pass 3 note: 'Only the human changes the goal set' contradicted the axiom's own case of an agent commit made anyway, leaving the guard's clauses vacuous.

payload.proposed_statement: Under the declarations in effect, a measured belief -- the posterior over a contract slice -- changes only through belief-eligible evidence, as DEF-belief-eligible defines it; a statement by an agent or a human carries zero weight in it.
payload.reason: Pass 4 note: committing a declaration (an acceptance rule, a removed test) changes beliefs by design, which the axiom as stated forbade. It governs belief under fixed declarations; changing those is the commit's business.

payload.proposed_statement: Every branch is a design and every design a branch, and adopting one is a decision on that branch under a policy criterion; the state that criterion requires of the branch's evidence is the state the design's policy requires. A design is adopted only while the measurement it cites agrees with it. The measurement a design cites is each contract its derivation rule names, each read on its own; it agrees with the design exactly when every one of them reads in the required state, and contradicts it exactly when one reads refuted where the required state is another. A design whose cited measurement contradicts it is rejected, and one whose cited measurement does not agree, is absent or cannot be read is not adopted.
payload.reason: Pass 4 gap: only 'a design is a branch' was stated; the gate needs every branch to be a design.

payload.proposed_statement: A project that enables the plugin at a version runs the release that plugin's manifest names, as it was published. Every server the plugin starts measures that project and no other: the only declarations and ledger it reads are that project's, and the only tests it runs are that project's, in that project's environment, not in the harness's own.
payload.reason: Pass 4 gap: the branch speaks of any declared test a server runs; the axiom must say a server reads no other declarations.

payload.proposed_statement: Under the declarations in effect, a record with provenance asserted cannot change any measured belief.
payload.reason: Follows AXM-no-belief-write-path's scoping to the declarations in effect.

payload.proposed_statement: Contract state: The state a contract reads in, where a design cites it: the weakest state among its slices, refuted weakest, then stale, contested, insufficient and supported; and no evidence when it has no slice. A policy criterion requires one of the five slice states, never no evidence.
payload.reason: Pass 5 gap: a criterion requiring 'no evidence' left 'absent' ambiguous. The declarations already refuse that criterion (BAD_CRITERION); the definition now says so.

payload.proposed_statement: Every measured record carries a reference to the artifact the server captured and that artifact's hash. Its metrics come from that artifact -- or, for a test that declares the metric passed and whose run wrote none, from the exit code the server captured -- and a record that lacks a metric its contract's rule reads is excluded, never given a value.
payload.reason: Pass 5 gap, and a disagreement with the code: the runner does synthesise passed from the exit code for a test that declares it; the claim said no metric is ever synthesised. It now says what the runner does, and what a measured record holds.

payload.proposed_statement: Belief-eligible evidence: A trial record with provenance measured -- the server ran a declared test, captured its artifact with the artifact's hash, and took the record's metrics from that artifact, or, where the run wrote none and its test declares the metric passed, took passed alone from the exit code the server captured -- or imported -- brought in with its source, an artifact and the artifact's hash -- and in either case recorded against a contract that a declared test can measure. Every record carries exactly one provenance: measured, imported or asserted. A record that is neither measured nor imported, a note among them, is asserted.
payload.reason: Pass 6 note: DEF-belief-eligible took metrics only from the artifact, while DEF-measured-record and the runner take passed from the exit code when the run wrote none -- so the two definitions disagreed on those records, and the code counted what the theory excluded.

payload.proposed_statement: Only committed declarations reach the belief model; under the declarations in effect, no evidence recorded against a contract that no declared test can measure moves a measured belief; and making an edit to a declaration file, and nothing else, changes no verdict the servers report.
payload.reason: Pass 7 gap TRL-0281: clause (b) dropped the 'under the declarations in effect' scope its derivation uses, so a test declared later made an earlier import count.

payload.proposed_statement: Set-aside record: A trial record is set aside exactly when its validity, after the amendments appended to it, is anything other than valid -- quarantined, invalid or superseded. A set-aside record moves no measured belief. A record counts exactly when it is not set aside.
payload.reason: Pass on BRN-audit-blocks-what-counts, note 1: 'a record that is not set aside counts' stated one direction; the derivation uses both.

payload.proposed_statement: Audit: The audit re-checks every artifact and every stamp that a measured or imported record rests on, whether or not that record counts, and makes a finding for each it can no longer audit. An artifact or stamp can no longer be audited exactly when the artifact is missing or no longer matches the hash recorded for it, or the stamp is missing or no longer matches the digest a trial resting on it recorded.
payload.reason: TRL-0296: a failed re-check was not said to produce a finding; and 'the digest its trials recorded' did not say which trial's.

payload.proposed_statement: Set-aside record: A trial record is set aside exactly when its validity, after the amendments appended to it, is anything other than valid -- quarantined, invalid or superseded. A set-aside record moves no measured belief. A trial record counts exactly when it is not set aside.
payload.reason: Wording note: 'counts' was defined for any record while 'set aside' is defined for trial records.

payload.proposed_statement: At every revision, every code link is reported as aligned exactly when it is aligned, and otherwise as not aligned, with why; and every mention, in a comment or docstring of a scanned file that does not declare its ids foreign, of an id that names no node in the declared graph at that revision and no code region is reported. Producing these reports changes no proof state and no measured belief.
payload.reason: TRL-0307..0309 refuted BRN-links-stale-when-either-side-moves: the axiom promised a report for every link but not that the report is right, and it covered every mention while files marked tdlp:foreign-ids set theirs aside.

payload.proposed_statement: A scanned file at a revision is a Python source file git tracks at that revision outside the ledger directories. A code link is a relation of kind implements, uses or checks, declared in comments of a scanned file at a revision, from a delimited region of that file to a node, carrying two pins: a body pin on the region and a claim pin on the relation. A relation of kind motivated-by asserts no correspondence and is not a code link. A region's body digest is determined by its code with comments and layout set aside, and differs whenever that code differs. The declared graph at a revision is the premise graph DEF-premise-graph describes, built from the declarations committed at that revision with no staged proposal. A node's claim digest at a revision is determined by the fingerprints, as DEF-current-trial uses them, of the node and of every node it depends on in the declared graph at that revision, and differs whenever any of those differs or the set of nodes it depends on differs. A pin is taken by recording the digest it names for the code and the claim as they stand, so it equals that digest for them. A file that declares tdlp:foreign-ids names ids of the projects it builds; its mentions are not mentions of this project's nodes. A code link is a declared relationship: it is not a trial and not a record in the ledger.
payload.reason: The verifier's gaps: scope to scanned files, a declared graph defined at any revision, pins equal to their digest when taken; and the code's own boundaries (motivated-by, foreign-ids) stated.

payload.proposed_statement: A code link is aligned at a revision exactly when its region is well formed and its id is carried by no other region there, its node is in the declared graph at that revision, its body pin equals the region's body digest at that revision, and its claim pin equals the node's claim digest at that revision.
payload.reason: "in the premise graph at that revision" becomes "in the declared graph": the premise graph is defined only at the head revision, with the ledger's staged proposals.

payload.proposed_statement: What taking a snapshot of a project returns and writes. Taking one resolves the project's head revision to one commit before it reads any declaration, names that commit and no other revision, and takes every declaration it shows from that commit and from no other version of it; a declaration file whose working copy differs from that commit it names as carrying uncommitted edits, which it does not show. It builds the premise graph as DEF-premise-graph defines it, from that commit's declarations and the proposals staged in the ledger as the snapshot read it, and every proposal it shows is the one staged for that id in the ledger as the snapshot read it. For each lemma and branch in that build it shows the proof state DEF-proof-state gives that node in that build, and no other. Beside them it lists the issues the declaration loaders and the build report, and the gaps the joined graph shows: an axiom naming no goal, a goal no axiom names, a component with code that no declared branch governs, an interface or goal no branch governs, and an axiom or definition nothing rests on. Beside each axiom, definition, lemma and branch it shows the code regions linked to that node in the scanned files of that commit, each with its link's state as DEF-aligned-link gives it at that commit, and it lists the tags and mentions the code-link scan of that commit reports as broken and the links it reports as not aligned; a code region is never a node or an edge of the premise graph it shows. It shows no state for a contract and reads no evidence record. Taking a snapshot appends no record to the ledger -- no trial, amendment, note, event or decision, of any provenance -- changes no declaration, makes no commit and does not move the head revision. Besides the report it returns, it writes two files and nothing else: its page, and a file that keeps git from tracking the directory both are in. That directory holds no declaration file and no part of the ledger, and where a component's code claims either file, or a declared test names either on its run line or among what it reads, the snapshot writes nothing.
payload.reason: 0.7.2 made the snapshot show each node's code regions with their link state, and the code-link scan's broken tags and unaligned links among its issues; DEF-snapshot listed what a snapshot shows and said nothing of either. The definition now says what the page does.
